prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1289; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in on the roadway in Pearland, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your full name and the best number to reach you.

A: I'd rather keep my personal details off the record for now, but you can reach me through the number already on file.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe what happened leading up to the collision?

A: I was stopped at a red light in the right lane. The traffic had been moving slowly, and I had come to a complete stop. I felt a hard jolt from behind and my head snapped forward and back.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt at the time?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did you notice the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Not really. I was looking ahead at the light. I didn't see it coming until right before it hit.

Q: Did you get out of your vehicle at the scene, and did you speak with the other driver?

A: I got out to look at the rear bumper. The other driver said they had been looking at their phone and didn't brake in time. We exchanged insurance information.

Q: Have you sought any medical treatment since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care the same evening. They diagnosed a neck strain and gave me muscle relaxers and told me to rest and apply ice.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. My neck is stiff, especially in the mornings, and turning my head to the left causes pain. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I'm hoping to get my vehicle repaired soon.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
